topology: Two PCs on PE1 and two servers on PE2 form BLUE and RED tenants. Both tenants reuse client192.168.10.0/24, transit10.0.0.0/30 and server192.168.20.0/24. One physical PE1 Gi0/1 to PE2 Gi0/1 link carries tagged subinterfaces110 and120. Unique BLUE/RED diagnostic loopbacks on PE2 permit real cross-tenant negative tests.
implemented: Eighth ENARSI Layer 3 Technologies entry with independent practice/completed factories, six-row plan, staged guide, tested IOS/Windows reference and verification commands, accurate accessible counts and current-site domain/path/query permalinks. All previous catalog entries remain available.

Both routers begin enabled and unnumbered. Learners define BLUE/RED IPv4 address families, bind access and transit subinterfaces before assigning overlapping addresses, and add fully specified scoped forward/return static routes. No route distinguishers, route targets, MPLS or BGP are required for this static VRF-Lite exercise.

Scoped CEF lookups must resolve the same server IP through separate logical egress interfaces and next-hop contexts. The physical parent stays enabled, unnumbered and global, while matching wire tags select each receiving subinterface and local routing table. VRF names are local identifiers, not a packet-header field.

Bidirectional host traffic correlates three actual requests and delivered parent-linked replies per direction with the correct client/server node identities and tagged physical transit frames. Explicit router-originated ping vrf BLUE and RED probes are independently required. Matching IP strings or fewer than three replies cannot fabricate delivery.

Separate dynamic ARP rows are correlated with received tagged ARP request/reply source IP and MAC evidence in the appropriate VRF/subinterface contexts. Passive request learning is accepted; different MAC values are not required because real subinterfaces can share one hardware MAC.

Both PCs must receive complete actual HTTP200 responses from different intended tenant servers at the same URL. The full body and server transaction identity must match BLUE/RED, not merely a TCP or HTTP success counter.

Each PC must reach its own unique PE2 loopback and observe three actual No route drops toward the other tenant loopback in its local ingress VRF. PE1 must separately fail three unqualified probes in the real global table while tenant traffic works; an undefined VRF or a general outage cannot stand in for isolation.

The BLUE tag exercise requires a PE2 tag111 mismatch, real PE1 VLAN110 ARP attempts and BLUE resolution failures, successful RED delivery, restoration to110 and fresh delivered replies from both clients. The missing-route exercise requires actual BLUE No route drops with RED success before restoring the exact scoped /24 and fresh traffic.

The access-binding exercise removes PE1 BLUE VRF membership, verifies IOS clears the IPv4 address, and requires real BLUE gateway/route failure while RED works. Rebinding alone leaves the address absent; both binding and address must be restored before fresh tenant replies earn the repair. Native tests cover warm and cold host ARP.

Fifteen tasks combine six live configuration/state/save goals and nine observed outcomes. Practice starts0/15. The completed reference supplies6/15 without invented packets, ARP rows, HTTP transactions or incidents. Earned observations survive portable YAML export/import, while current topology, exact configuration, health and startup equality remain live.

Per-attempt epochs and normal simulator notifications capture CLI evidence with a closed guide. Configuration-only toggles, fake neighbors, wrong server identity, incomplete topology, global-route shortcuts and missing return routes fail closed. No simulation engine, protocol implementation, UI styling, terminal theme or artwork changed.
scope: IOS IPv4 VRF-Lite using two routers, static routing and one shared 802.1Q cable. Native/browser validation does not claim a fresh CML capture. This lab does not configure MPLS L3VPNs, MP-BGP, inter-VRF leaking, dynamic routing per VRF, IPv6 or NX-OS.
